item: The scrypt cost read from an encrypted file's header is bounded to what every writer has produced and anything else is refused as a malformed header before any work
summary: _derive took n, r and p from the OOENC1/OOENC2 header with no bound, so a crafted file could ask for an enormous scrypt (memory n*r*128 bytes). Every container this app has written carries exactly (2**15, 8, 1) (git history), so the reader accepts exactly that and raises EncryptionError(malformed encrypted header) before deriving a key. The bound protects the memory of one derivation, 32 MiB by formula, measured 32.8 MiB peak growth and 0.11 s. Tested with oversize and undersize headers on both formats (red without; no key is derived), and the writers still round trip. A build that writes other parameters must add them in the commit that adds it. The accepted tuple is the writers' own constant (_N, _R, _P), shared by writer and reader, so changing the writer's cost changes what the reader accepts and a build cannot refuse its own new files; a test derives the tuple from the constant rather than a literal and pins both directions.
